options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.uvls.packageFallback
options.description:
When enabled, the language server package will be added to the end of the `PATH` _(suffix)_ instead of the beginning _(prefix)_.

This can be useful if you want local versions of the language server (e.g. from a devshell) to override the Nixvim version.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.uvls.rootMarkers
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
A list of files that mark the root of the project/workspace.

Vim's LSP will try to share the same language server instance for all
buffers matching `filetypes` within the same project.

A new server instance is only spawned when opening a buffer with a
different project root.

See `:h lsp-config` and `:h vim.fs.root()`.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.uvls.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.description: The settings for this LSP.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.vespa_ls.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable https://github.com/vespa-engine/vespa/tree/master/integration/schema-language-server
Vespa Language Server provides LSP features such as completion,
diagnostics, and go-to-definition for Vespa schema files (`.sd`),
profile files (`.profile`), and YQL query files (`.yql`). This language
server requires Java 17 or higher. You can build the jar from source.
You can override the default command by manually configuring it like
this:

``` lua
vim.lsp.config('vespa_ls', {
  cmd = { 'java', '-jar', '/path/to/vespa-language-server.jar' },
})
```

The project root is determined based on the presence of a `.git`
directory. To make Neovim recognize the proper filetypes, add the
following setting in `init.lua`: vim.filetype.add { extension = {
profile = 'sd', sd = 'sd', yql = 'yql', }, }.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.vhdl_ls.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable Install vhdl_ls from https://github.com/VHDL-LS/rust_hdl and add it to
path Configuration The language server needs to know your library
mapping to perform full analysis of the code. For this it uses a
configuration file in the TOML format named vhdl_ls.toml. vhdl_ls will
load configuration files in the following order of priority (first to
last): A file named .vhdl_ls.toml in the user home folder. A file name
from the VHDL_LS_CONFIG environment variable. A file named vhdl_ls.toml
in the workspace root. Settings in a later files overwrites those from
previously loaded files. Example vhdl_ls.toml

    # File names are either absolute or relative to the parent folder of the vhdl_ls.toml file
    [libraries]
    lib2.files = [
      'pkg2.vhd',
    ]
    lib1.files = [
      'pkg1.vhd',
      'tb_ent.vhd'
    ].

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.vtsls.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable https://github.com/yioneko/vtsls `vtsls` can be installed with npm:

``` sh
npm install -g @vtsls/language-server
```

To configure a TypeScript project, add a
[`tsconfig.json`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/tsconfig-json.html)
or
[`jsconfig.json`](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/jsconfig)
to the root of your project. \### Vue support Since v3.0.0, the Vue
language server requires `vtsls` to support TypeScript.

    -- If you are using mason.nvim, you can get the ts_plugin_path like this
    -- For Mason v1,
    -- local mason_registry = require('mason-registry')
    -- local vue_language_server_path = mason_registry.get_package('vue-language-server'):get_install_path() .. '/node_modules/@vue/language-server'
    -- For Mason v2,
    -- local vue_language_server_path = vim.fn.expand '$MASON/packages' .. '/vue-language-server' .. '/node_modules/@vue/language-server'
    -- or even
    -- local vue_language_server_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. "/mason/packages/vue-language-server/node_modules/@vue/language-server"
    local vue_language_server_path = '/path/to/@vue/language-server'
    local vue_plugin = {
      name = '@vue/typescript-plugin',
      location = vue_language_server_path,
      languages = { 'vue' },
      configNamespace = 'typescript',
    }
    vim.lsp.config('vtsls', {
      settings = {
        vtsls = {
          tsserver = {
            globalPlugins = {
              vue_plugin,
            },
          },
        },
      },
      filetypes = { 'typescript', 'javascript', 'javascriptreact', 'typescriptreact', 'vue' },
    })

- `location` MUST be defined. If the plugin is installed in
  `node_modules`, `location` can have any value.
- `languages` must include vue even if it is listed in filetypes.
- `filetypes` is extended here to include Vue SFC. You must make sure
  the Vue language server is setup. For example,

<!-- -->

    vim.lsp.enable('vue_ls')

See `vue_ls` section and
https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/wiki/Neovim for more
information. \### Monorepo support `vtsls` supports monorepos by
default. It will automatically find the `tsconfig.json` or
`jsconfig.json` corresponding to the package you are working on. This
works without the need of spawning multiple instances of `vtsls`, saving
memory. It is recommended to use the same version of TypeScript in all
packages, and therefore have it available in your workspace root. The
location of the TypeScript binary will be determined automatically, but
only once. This includes the same Deno-excluding logic from `ts_ls`. It
is not recommended to enable both `vtsls` and `ts_ls` at the same time!.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.vtsls.extraOptions
options.description: Extra options for the vtsls language server.

options.title: plugins.lsp.servers.vue_ls.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/tree/master/packages/language-server
The official language server for Vue It can be installed via npm:

``` sh
npm install -g @vue/language-server
```

The language server only supports Vue 3 projects by default. For Vue 2
projects, [additional
configuration](https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/blob/master/extensions/vscode/README.md?plain=1#L19)
are required. The Vue language server works in "hybrid mode" that
exclusively manages the CSS/HTML sections. You need the `vtsls` server
with the `@vue/typescript-plugin` plugin to support TypeScript in `.vue`
files. See `vtsls` section and
https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/wiki/Neovim for more
information. NOTE: Since v3.0.0, the Vue Language Server [no longer
supports takeover
mode](https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/pull/5248)..

options.title: plugins.luasnip.settings.parser_nested_assembler
options.description: Override the default behavior of inserting a choiceNode containing the nested snippet and an empty insertNode for nested placeholders.
options.default:
`null`

_Plugin default:_
```
lib.nixvim.mkRaw ''
  function(pos, snip)
    local iNode = require("luasnip.nodes.insertNode")
    local cNode = require("luasnip.nodes.choiceNode")
  
    modify_nodes(snip)
    snip:init_nodes()
    snip.pos = nil
  
    return cNode.C(pos, { snip, iNode.I(nil, { "" }) })
  end
''
```

- `foo_bar = 1` -> `:setglobal magma_foo_bar=1`
- `hello = "world"` -> `:setglobal magma_hello="world"`

- `other_toggle = false` -> `:setglobal nomagma_other_toggle`

options.title: plugins.magma-nvim.settings.automatically_open_output
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If this is true, then whenever you have an active cell its output window will be
automatically shown.

If this is false, then the output window will only be automatically shown when you've just
evaluated the code.
So, if you take your cursor out of the cell, and then come back, the output window won't be
opened (but the cell will be highlighted).
This means that there will be nothing covering your code.
You can then open the output window at will using `:MagmaShowOutput`.

options.description: The highlight group to be used for highlighting cells.

options.title: plugins.magma-nvim.settings.image_provider
options.type: null or one of "none", "ueberzug", "kitty" or raw lua code
options.description:
This configures how to display images. The following options are available:
  - "none" -- don't show images.
  - "ueberzug" -- use Ueberzug to display images.
  - "kitty" -- use the Kitty protocol to display images.

options.title: plugins.magma-nvim.settings.output_window_borders
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If this is true, then the output window will have rounded borders.
If it is false, it will have no borders.

options.title: plugins.magma-nvim.settings.save_path
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Where to save/load with `:MagmaSave` and `:MagmaLoad` (with no parameters).
The generated file is placed in this directory, with the filename itself being the
buffer's name, with `%` replaced by `%%` and `/` replaced by `%`, and postfixed with the
extension `.json`.

options.title: plugins.magma-nvim.settings.show_mimetype_debug
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If this is true, then before any non-iostream output chunk, Magma shows the mimetypes it
received for it.
This is meant for debugging and adding new mimetypes.

options.description:

plugin would only call it conditionally.

options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.description: Options provided to the `require('neoclip').setup` function.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.content_spec_column
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description: Can be set to `true` to use instead of the preview.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.continuous_sync
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If set to `true`, the runtime history is synced with the persistent storage everytime it's
changed or queried.

If you often use multiple sessions in parallel and wants the history synced you might want to
enable this.

Off by default; it can cause delays because the history file is written everytime you yank
something.
Although, in practice no real slowdowns were noticed.

Alternatively see `db_pull` and `db_push` functions in the
[README](https://github.com/AckslD/nvim-neoclip.lua#custom-actions).

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.db_path
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The path to the sqlite database to store history if `enable_persistent_history=true`.
Defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/nvim/databases/neoclip.sqlite3`.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.default_register
options.type: null or string or list of string
options.description:
What register to use by default when not specified (e.g. `Telescope neoclip`).
Can be a string such as `"\""` (single register) or a table of strings such as
`["\"" "+" "*"]`.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.default_register_macros
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description: What register to use for macros by default when not specified (e.g. `Telescope macroscope`).

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.disable_keycodes_parsing
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If set to true, macroscope will display the internal byte representation, instead of a proper
string that can be used in a map.

So a macro like `"one<CR>two"` will be displayed as `"one\ntwo"`.
It will only show the type and number of lines next to the first line of the entry.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.enable_macro_history
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If true (default) any recorded macro will be saved, see
[macros](https://github.com/AckslD/nvim-neoclip.lua#macros).

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.enable_persistent_history
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If set to `true` the history is stored on `VimLeavePre` using `sqlite.lua` and lazy loaded when
querying.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.filter
options.description:
A function to filter what entries to store (default all are stored).
This function filter should return `true` (include the yanked entry) or `false` (don't include
it) based on a table as the only argument, which has the following keys:

- `event`: The event from `TextYankPost` (see ``:help TextYankPost` for which keys it contains).
- `filetype`: The filetype of the buffer where the yank happened.
- `buffer_name`: The name of the buffer where the yank happened.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.history
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: The max number of entries to store.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.keys.fzf
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Keys to use for the `fzf` picker.
Only insert mode is supported and fzf-style key-syntax needs to be used.
You can also use the `custom` entry to specify custom actions to take on certain
key-presses, see
[here](https://github.com/AckslD/nvim-neoclip.lua?tab=readme-ov-file#custom-actions) for
more details.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.keys.telescope
options.type: null or (attribute set of ((attribute set of anything) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Keys to use for the `telescope` picker.
Normal key-syntax is supported and both insert `i` and normal mode `n`.
You can also use the `custom` entry to specify custom actions to take on certain
key-presses, see
[here](https://github.com/AckslD/nvim-neoclip.lua?tab=readme-ov-file#custom-actions) for
more details.

NOTE: these are only set in the telescope buffer and you need to setup your own keybindings to for example open telescope.

options.title: plugins.neoclip.settings.length_limit
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
The max number of characters of an entry to be stored (default 1MiB).
If the length of the yanked string is larger than the limit, it will not be stored.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.format
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Formatters are used in format definitions.

Noice includes the following formatters:

- `level`: message level with optional icon and hl_group per level
- `text`: any text with optional hl_group
- `title`: message title with optional hl_group
- `event`: message event with optional hl_group
- `kind`: message kind with optional hl_group
- `date`: formatted date with optional date format string
- `message`: message content itself with optional hl_group to override message highlights
- `confirm`: only useful for confirm messages. Will format the choices as buttons.
- `cmdline`: will render the cmdline in the message that generated the message.
- `progress`: progress bar used by lsp progress
- `spinner`: spinners used by lsp progress
- `data`: render any custom data from Message.opts. Useful in combination with the opts passed to vim.notify

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.notify.enabled
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Enable notification handling.

Noice can be used as `vim.notify` so you can route any notification like other messages.

Notification messages have their level and other properties set.
event is always "notify" and kind can be any log level as a string.

The default routes will forward notifications to nvim-notify.
Benefit of using Noice for this is the routing and consistent history view.

options.description: Notify backend to use.

options.description: Backend to use to show regular cmdline completions.

options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description: Enable the Noice popupmenu UI.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.popupmenu.kindIcons
options.type: null or boolean or attribute set of anything or raw lua code
options.description: Icons for completion item kinds. Set to `false` to disable icons.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.presets
options.description:
You can enable a preset by setting it to `true`, or a table that will override
the preset config.

You can also add custom presets that you can enable/disable with `enabled=true`.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.redirect
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Default options for `require('noice').redirect`.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.routes
options.type: null or (list of ((attribute set of anything) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Route options can be any of the view options or `skip` or `stop`.

A route has a filter, view and optional opts attribute.

- `view`: one of the views (built-in or custom)
- `filter` a filter for messages matching this route
- `opts`: options for the view and the route

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.smart_move.enabled
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Noice tries to move out of the way of existing floating windows.
You can disable this behaviour here.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.smart_move.excluded_filetypes
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Filetypes that shouldn't trigger smart move.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.status
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Noice comes with the following statusline components:

- `ruler`
- `message`: last line of the last message (event=show_msg)
- `command`: showcmd
- `mode`: showmode (@recording messages)
- `search`: search count messages

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.throttle
options.type: null or signed integer or floating point number or raw lua code
options.description:
How frequently does Noice need to check for ui updates?

This has no effect when in blocking mode.

options.title: plugins.noice.settings.views
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
A view is a combination of a backend and options.

Noice comes with the following built-in backends:

 - `popup`: powered by nui.nvim
 - `split`: powered by nui.nvim
 - `notify`: powered by nvim-notify
 - `virtualtext`: shows the message as virtualtext (for example for search_count)
 - `mini`: similar to notifier.nvim & fidget.nvim
 - `notify_send`: generate a desktop notification

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.cmd
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Defines the command used to start the null-ls server.
If you do not have an `nvim` binary available on your `$PATH`,
you should change this to an absolute path to the binary.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.debounce
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
The `debounce` setting controls the amount of time between the last change to a
buffer and the next `textDocument/didChange` notification. These notifications
cause null-ls to generate diagnostics, so this setting indirectly controls the
rate of diagnostic generation (affected by `update_in_insert`, described below).

Lowering `debounce` will result in quicker diagnostic refreshes at the cost of running
diagnostic sources more frequently, which can affect performance.
The default value should be enough to provide near-instantaneous feedback from most sources
without unnecessary resource usage.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.debug
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Displays all possible log messages and writes them to the null-ls log, which you
can view with the command `:NullLsLog`. This option can slow down Neovim, so
it's strongly recommended to disable it for normal use.

`debug = true` is the same as setting `log_level` to `"trace"`.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.default_timeout
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
Sets the amount of time (in milliseconds) after which built-in sources will time out.
Note that built-in sources can define their own timeout period and that users can override the
timeout period on a per-source basis, too
(see [BUILTIN_CONFIG.md](https://github.com/nvimtools/none-ls.nvim/blob/main/doc/BUILTIN_CONFIG.md)).

Specifying a timeout with a value less than zero will prevent commands from timing out.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.diagnostic_config
options.type: null or (attribute set) or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Specifies diagnostic display options for null-ls sources, as described in
`:help vim.diagnostic.config()`.
(null-ls uses separate namespaces for each source,
so server-wide configuration will not work as expected.)

You can also configure `diagnostic_config` per built-in by using the `with` method, described
in [BUILTIN_CONFIG](https://github.com/nvimtools/none-ls.nvim/blob/main/doc/BUILTIN_CONFIG.md).

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.diagnostics_format
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Sets the default format used for diagnostics. The plugin will replace the following special
components with the relevant diagnostic information:

- `#{m}`: message
- `#{s}`: source name (defaults to `null-ls` if not specified)
- `#{c}`: code (if available)

For example, setting `diagnostics_format` to the following:

```lua
  diagnostics_format = "[#{c}] #{m} (#{s})"
```

Formats diagnostics as follows:

```txt
  [2148] Tips depend on target shell and yours is unknown. Add a shebang or a 'shell' directive. (shellcheck)
```

  You can also configure `diagnostics_format` per built-in by using the `with`
  method, described in [BUILTIN_CONFIG](https://github.com/nvimtools/none-ls.nvim/blob/main/doc/BUILTIN_CONFIG.md).

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.fallback_severity
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
Defines the severity used when a diagnostic source does not explicitly define a severity.
See `:help diagnostic-severity` for available values.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.log_level
options.type: null or one of "off", "error", "warn", "info", "debug", "trace" or raw lua code
options.description:
Enables or disables logging to file.

Plugin logs messages on several logging levels to following destinations:
- file, can be inspected by `:NullLsLog`.
- neovim's notification area.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.notify_format
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Sets the default format for `vim.notify()` messages.
Can be used to customize 3rd party notification plugins like
[nvim-notify](https://github.com/rcarriga/nvim-notify).

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.on_attach
options.description:
Defines an `on_attach` callback to run whenever null-ls attaches to a buffer.
If you have a common `on_attach` you're using for LSP servers, you can reuse that here,
use a custom callback for null-ls, or leave this undefined.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.on_exit
options.description: Defines an `on_exit` callback to run when the null-ls client exits.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.on_init
options.description:
Defines an `on_init` callback to run when null-ls initializes.
From here, you can make changes to the client (the first argument)
or `initialize_result` (the second argument, which as of now is not used).

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.root_dir
options.description:
Determines the root of the null-ls server. On startup, null-ls will call
`root_dir` with the full path to the first file that null-ls attaches to.

If `root_dir` returns `nil`, the root will resolve to the current working directory.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.root_dir_async
options.description:
Like `root_dir` but also accepts a callback parameter allowing it to be
asynchronous. Overwrites `root_dir` when present.

For a utility that asynchronously finds a matching file, see `utils.root_pattern_async`.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.should_attach
options.description:
A user-defined function that controls whether to enable null-ls for a given
buffer. Receives `bufnr` as its first argument.

To cut down potentially expensive calls, null-ls will call `should_attach` after
its own internal checks pass, so it's not guaranteed to run on each new buffer.

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.temp_dir
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Defines the directory used to create temporary files for sources that rely on
them (a workaround used for command-based sources that do not support `stdio`).

To maximize compatibility, null-ls defaults to creating temp files in the same
directory as the parent file. If this is causing issues, you can set it to
`/tmp` (or another appropriate directory) here. Otherwise, there is no need to
change this setting.

**Note**: some null-ls built-in sources expect temp files to exist within a
project for context and so will not work if this option changes.

You can also configure `temp_dir` per built-in by using the `with` method,
described in [BUILTIN_CONFIG](https://github.com/nvimtools/none-ls.nvim/blob/main/doc/BUILTIN_CONFIG.md).

options.title: plugins.none-ls.settings.update_in_insert
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Controls whether diagnostic sources run in insert mode. If set to `false`,
diagnostic sources will run upon exiting insert mode, which greatly improves
performance but can create a slight delay before diagnostics show up. Set this
to `true` if you don't experience performance issues with your sources.

Note that by default, Neovim will not display updated diagnostics in insert
mode. Together with the option above, you need to pass `update_in_insert = true`
to `vim.diagnostic.config` for diagnostics to work as expected. See
`:help vim.diagnostic.config` for more info.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.autoLoad
options.description: Whether to automatically load notebook-navigator when neovim starts.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.callSetup
options.description:
Whether to generate the standard `require('notebook-navigator').setup(...)` call for this plugin.

By default, this follows the plugin's built-in behavior. Set this to `false`
to disable the generated setup call, or to `true` to force it even when the
plugin would only call it conditionally.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.enable
options.description: Whether to enable notebook-navigator.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.lazyLoad
options.description:
Lazy-load settings for notebook-navigator.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental option and may not work as expected with all plugins.
> The API may change without notice.
> Please report any issues you encounter.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.lazyLoad.enable
options.description: lazy-loading for notebook-navigator

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.lazyLoad.settings
options.description:
Lazy provider configuration settings.

Check your lazy loading provider's documentation on settings to configure.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.luaConfig
options.description: The plugin's lua configuration

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.luaConfig.content
options.description:
Configuration of the plugin.

If `pre` and/or `post` are non-null, they will be merged using the order priorities
300 and 300
respectively.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.luaConfig.post
options.description:
Lua code inserted at the end of the plugin's configuration.
This is the same as using `lib.nixvim.utils.mkAfterSection` when defining `content`.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.luaConfig.pre
options.description:
Lua code inserted at the start of the plugin's configuration.
This is the same as using `lib.nixvim.utils.mkBeforeSection` when defining `content`.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.package
options.description: The notebook-navigator package to use.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.description: Options provided to the `require('notebook-navigator').setup` function.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.activate_hydra_keys
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
If not `nil` the keymap defined in the string will activate the hydra head.
If you don't want to use hydra you don't need to install it either.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.cell_highlight_group
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description: For use with `mini.hipatterns` to highlight cell markers.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.cell_markers
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Code cell marker.

Cells start with the marker and end either at the beginning of the next cell or at the end of
the file.

By default, uses language-specific double percent comments like `# %%`.
This can be overridden for each language with this setting.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.hydra_keys
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Mappings while the hydra head is active.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.repl_provider
options.type: null or one of "auto", "iron", "molten", "toggleterm" or raw lua code
options.description:
The repl plugin with which to interface.

Current options:
- "iron" for iron.nvim,
- "toggleterm" for toggleterm.nvim,
- "molten" for molten-nvim
- "auto" which checks which of the above are installed

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.show_hydra_hint
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If `true` a hint panel will be shown when the hydra head is active.
If `false` you get a minimalistic hint on the command line.

options.title: plugins.notebook-navigator.settings.syntax_highlight
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:

If you don't want to install `mini.hipattners` or enjoy a more minimalistic look.

options.example:
{
  fold_virt_text_handler = ''
    function(virtText, lnum, endLnum, width, truncate)
      local newVirtText = {}
      local suffix = ('  %d '):format(endLnum - lnum)
      local sufWidth = vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(suffix)
      local targetWidth = width - sufWidth
      local curWidth = 0
      for _, chunk in ipairs(virtText) do
        local chunkText = chunk[1]
        local chunkWidth = vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(chunkText)
        if targetWidth > curWidth + chunkWidth then
          table.insert(newVirtText, chunk)
        else
          chunkText = truncate(chunkText, targetWidth - curWidth)
          local hlGroup = chunk[2]
          table.insert(newVirtText, {chunkText, hlGroup})
          chunkWidth = vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(chunkText)
          -- str width returned from truncate() may less than 2nd argument, need padding
          if curWidth + chunkWidth < targetWidth then
            suffix = suffix .. (' '):rep(targetWidth - curWidth - chunkWidth)
          end
          break
        end
        curWidth = curWidth + chunkWidth
      end
      table.insert(newVirtText, {suffix, 'MoreMsg'})
      return newVirtText
    end
  '';
  provider_selector = ''
    function(bufnr, filetype, buftype)
      local ftMap = {
        vim = "indent",
        python = {"indent"},
        git = ""
      }
    
     return ftMap[filetype]
    end
  '';
}

options.title: plugins.rainbow-delimiters.strategy
options.type: null or (attribute set of (one of "global", "local", "noop" or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Attrs mapping Tree-sitter language names to strategies.
See `|rb-delimiters-strategy|` for more information about strategies.
This option adds definitions to `plugins.rainbow-delimiters.settings.strategy` wrapped with required Lua code.
options.example:
```nix
{
  # Use global strategy by default
  "" = "global";

  # Use local for HTML
  html = "local";

  # Pick the strategy for LaTeX dynamically based on the buffer size
  latex.__raw = ''
    function()
      -- Disabled for very large files, global strategy for large files,
      -- local strategy otherwise
      if vim.fn.line('$') > 10000 then
          return nil
      elseif vim.fn.line('$') > 1000 then
          return require 'rainbow-delimiters'.strategy['global']
      end
      return require 'rainbow-delimiters'.strategy['local']
    end
  '';
}
```

options.description:
In any custom print var statement, it is possible to optionally add a **max of two `%s` patterns**, which is where the debug path and
the actual variable reference will go, respectively. To add a literal `"%s"` to the string, escape the sequence like this: `%%s`.
For an example custom print var statement, go to [this folder][folder], select your language, and view `multiple-statements/print_var.config`.

Note: if you have multiple custom statements, the plugin will prompt for which one should be inserted.
If you just have one custom statement in your config, it will override the default automatically.

Example:

```nix
  {
    # add a custom print var statement for cpp
    cpp = [ "printf(\"a custom statement %%s %s\", %s)" ];
  }
```

[folder]: https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/refactoring.nvim/blob/master/lua/refactoring/tests/debug/print_var

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.debounce
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
This is meant to space out how often this plugin parses the content of the viewport in
milliseconds to avoid causing too much lag while scrolling & editing.

For example if you hold `j` once you've scrolled far enough down you'll notice that there is
no longer any rendering happening.
Only once you've stopped scrolling for this debounce time will the plugin parse the viewport
and update the marks.
If you don't mind the lag or have a really fast system you can reduce this value to make the
plugin feel snappier.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.enabled
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
This lets you set whether the plugin should render documents from the start or not.
Useful if you want to use a command like `RenderMarkdown enable` to start rendering documents
rather than having it on by default.

There are ways to accomplish the same thing with the `lazy.nvim` `cmd` option, the point of
this feature is to be plugin manager agnostic.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.injections
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
This plugin works by iterating through the language trees of the current buffer and adding
marks for handled languages such as `markdown`.

For standard `markdown` files this is the entire file, however for other filetypes this
may be only specific sections.

This option allows users to define these sections within the plugin configuration as well
as allowing this plugin to provide logical defaults for a "batteries included" experience.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.max_file_size
options.type: null or floating point number or raw lua code
options.description:
The maximum file size that this plugin will attempt to render in megabytes.

This plugin only does rendering for what is visible within the viewport so the size of the
file does not directly impact its performance.
However large files in general are laggy enough hence this feature.

The size is only checked once when the file is opened and not after every update, so a file
that grows larger than this in the process of editing will continue to be rendered.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.overrides.buftype
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
This lets you set nearly all the options available at a `buftype` level.
Think of the top level configuration as the default where when the `buftype` match these
override values are used instead.
`filetype` takes precedence over `buftype`.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.overrides.filetype
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
This lets you set nearly all the options available at a `filetype` level.
Think of the top level configuration as the default where when the `filetype` match these
override values are used instead.
`filetype` takes precedence over `buftype`.

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.preset
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Allows you to set many different non default options with a single value.
You can view the values for these [here](https://github.com/MeanderingProgrammer/render-markdown.nvim/blob/main/lua/render-markdown/lib/presets.lua).

options.title: plugins.render-markdown.settings.win_options
options.type: null or (attribute set of ((open submodule of attribute set of anything) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Window options are used by the plugin to set different window level neovim option values
when rendering and when not rendering a file.

This is useful for 2 reasons:
- To allow options for rendering to be controlled by the plugin configuration so users
  don't need to set global or ftplugin options to make things work.
- Some option values are more useful for appearance and others are more useful while
  editing.

options.title: plugins.rustaceanvim.settings.server.auto_attach
options.type: null or lua function string or boolean
options.description:
Whether to automatically attach the LSP client.
Defaults to `true` if the `rust-analyzer` executable is found.

This can also be the definition of a function (`fun():boolean`).

Plugin default:
```lua
  function(bufnr)
    if #vim.bo[bufnr].buftype > 0 then
      return false
    end
    local path = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(bufnr)
    if not os.is_valid_file_path(path) then
      return false
    end
    local cmd = types.evaluate(RustaceanConfig.server.cmd)
```

This option is ignored for scrollview windows whose highlight group has `reverse` or `inverse`

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.bookmarks
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code or (attribute set) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
A list of files or directories to bookmark.
The list can contain two kinds of types.
Either a path (str) or an attrs where the key is the custom index and the value is the path.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.change_cmd
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The default command for switching directories.

Valid values:
- `cd`
- `lcd`
- `tcd`

Affects `change_to_dir` and `change_to_vcs_root`.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.change_to_dir
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
When opening a file or bookmark, change to its directory.

You want to disable this, if you're using `|'autochdir'|` as well.

NOTE: It defaults to `true`, because that was already the behaviour at the time this option was
introduced.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.change_to_vcs_root
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
When opening a file or bookmark, seek and change to the root directory of the VCS (if there is
one).

At the moment only git, hg, bzr and svn are supported.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.commands
options.type: null or (list of (string or attribute set of (string or list of string) or list of string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
A list of commands to execute on selection.
Leading colons are optional.
It supports optional custom indices and/or command descriptions.

Example:
```nix
[
  ":help reference"
  ["Vim Reference" "h ref"]
  {h = "h ref";}
  {m = ["My magical function" "call Magic()"];}
]
```

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.custom_footer
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Same as the custom header, but shown at the bottom of the startify buffer.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.custom_header
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Define your own header.

This option takes a `list of strings`, whereas each string will be put on its own line.
If it is a simple `string`, it should evaluate to a list of strings.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.custom_header_quotes
options.type: null or (list of ((list of string) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
If you don't set `custom_header`, the internal cowsay implementation with
predefined random quotes will be used.

To use your own quotes, set this option to a list of quotes. Each quote is
either another list or a `|Funcref|` (see `|expr-lambda|`) that returns a list.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.custom_indices
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Use any list of strings as indices instead of increasing numbers. If there are more startify
entries than actual items in the custom list, the remaining entries will be filled using the
default numbering scheme starting from 0.

Thus you can create your own indexing scheme that fits your keyboard layout.
You don't want to leave the home row, do you?!

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.disable_at_vimenter
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Don't run Startify at Vim startup.
You can still call it anytime via `:Startify`.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.enable_special
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description: Show `<empty buffer>` and `<quit>`.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.enable_unsafe
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Enable the option only in case you think Vim starts too slowly (because of `:Startify`) or if
you often edit files on remote filesystems.

It's called unsafe because it improves the time `:Startify` needs to execute by reducing the
amount of syscalls to the underlying operating system, but sacrifices the precision of shown
entries.

This could lead to inconsistencies in the shown `:Startify` entries (e.g. the same file could be
shown twice, because one time file was opened via absolute path and another time via symlink).

Currently this option does this:
- don't resolves symlinks (`readlink(2)`)
- don't check every file if it's readable (`stat(2)`)
- don't filter through the bookmark list

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.files_number
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: The number of files to list.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.fortune_use_unicode
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
By default, the fortune header uses ASCII characters, because they work for everyone.
If you set this option to `true` and your 'encoding' is "utf-8", Unicode box-drawing characters
will be used instead.

This is not the default, because users of East Asian languages often set 'ambiwidth' to "double"
or make their terminal emulator treat characters of ambiguous width as double width.
Both would make the drawn box look funny.

For more information: http://unicode.org/reports/tr11

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.lists
options.type: list of (lua code string or (open submodule of attribute set of anything))

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.padding_left
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: The number of spaces used for left padding.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.relative_path
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If the file is in or below the current working directory, use a relative path.
Otherwise an absolute path is used.
The latter prevents hard to grasp entries like `../../../../../foo`.

NOTE: This only applies to the "files" list, since the "dir" list is relative by nature.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_autoload
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If this option is enabled and you start Vim in a directory that contains a `Session.vim`,
that session will be loaded automatically.
Otherwise it will be shown as the top entry in the Startify buffer.

The same happens when you `|:cd|` to a directory that contains a `Session.vim` and execute
`|:Startify|`.

It also works if you open a bookmarked directory. See the `bookmarks` option.

This is great way to create a portable project folder!

NOTE: This option is affected by `session_delete_buffers`.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_before_save
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
This is a list of commands to be executed before saving a session.

Example: `["silent! tabdo NERDTreeClose"]`

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_delete_buffers
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Delete all buffers when loading or closing a session:
- When using `|startify-:SLoad|`.
- When using `|startify-:SClose|`.
- When using `session_autoload`.
- When choosing a session from the Startify buffer.

NOTE: Buffers with unsaved changes are silently ignored.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_dir
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description: The directory to save/load sessions to/from.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_number
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
The maximum number of sessions to display.
Makes the most sense together with `session_sort`.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_persistence
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Automatically update sessions in two cases:
- Before leaving Vim
- Before loading a new session via `:SLoad`

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_remove_lines
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Lines matching any of the patterns in this list, will be removed from the session file.

Example:
```nix
["setlocal" "winheight"]
```
Internally this simply does:
- `:global/setlocal/delete`
- `:global/winheight/delete`

So you can use any `|pattern|`.

NOTE: Take care not to mess up any expressions within the session file, otherwise you'll
probably get problems when trying to load it.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_savecmds
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Include a list of cmdline commands which Vim will run upon loading the session.

Example:
```nix
[
  "silent !pdfreader ~/latexproject/main.pdf &"
]
```

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_savevars
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Include a list of variables in here which you would like Startify to save into the session file
in addition to what Vim normally saves into the session file.

Example:
```nix
[
  "g:startify_session_savevars"
  "g:startify_session_savecmds"
  "g:random_plugin_use_feature"
]
```

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.session_sort
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Sort sessions by modification time (when the session files were written) rather than
alphabetically.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.skiplist
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
A list of Vim regular expressions that is used to filter recently used files.
See `|pattern.txt|` for what patterns can be used.

The following patterns are filtered by default:
- `'runtime/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'bundle/.*/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'plugged/.*/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'/.git/'`
- `'fugitiveblame$'`
- `escape(fnamemodify(resolve($VIMRUNTIME), ':p'), '\') .'doc/.*\.txt$'`

NOTE: Due to the nature of patterns, you can't just use "~/mysecret" but have to use
"$HOME .'/mysecret.txt'".
The former would do something entirely different: `|/\~|`.

NOTE: When using backslashes as path separators, escape them. Otherwise using
"C:\this\vim\path\is\problematic" would not match what you would expect, since `|/\v|` is a
pattern, too.

Example:
```nix
[
  "\.vimgolf"
  "^/tmp"
  "/project/.*/documentation"
]
```

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.skiplist_server
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Do not create the startify buffer, if this is a Vim server instance with a name contained in
this list.

Example: `["GVIM"]`

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.update_oldfiles
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Usually `|v:oldfiles|` only gets updated when Vim exits.
Using this option updates it on-the-fly, so that `:Startify` is always up-to-date.

options.title: plugins.startify.settings.use_env
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Show environment variables in path, if their name is shorter than their value.
See `|startify-colors|` for highlighting them.

`$PWD` and `$OLDPWD` are ignored.

options.description:
This option can be set values as `"LUA"|string[]|null`.
With the default value: `null`, it uses these way below to make entries for workspace
files.
It tries in order until it works successfully.

1. `rg -.g '!.git' --files`
2. `fdfind -Htf`
3. `fd -Htf`
4. Native Lua code (old way)

If you like another commands, set them to this option, like
```nix
  workspace_scan_cmd = ["find" "." "-type" "f"];
```

If you prefer Native Lua code, set `workspace_scan_cmd.__raw = "LUA"`.

options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
By default, if you zoom the tmux pane running vim and then attempt to navigate "past" the edge of the vim session, tmux will unzoom the pane.
This is the default tmux behavior, but may be confusing if you've become accustomed to navigation "wrapping" around the sides due to this plugin.

This option disables the unzooming behavior, keeping all navigation within vim until the tmux pane is explicitly unzoomed.

options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.no_mappings
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
By default `<C-h>`, `<C-j>`, `<C-k>`, `<C-l>`, & `<C-\\>`
are mapped to navigating left, down, up, right, & previous, respectively.

This option disables those default mappings being created.

You can use `plugins.tmux-navigator.keymaps` to define your own custom mappings.
You will also need to **update your tmux bindings** separately,
if you want them to match.

options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.no_wrap
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code

options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.preserve_zoom
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
As noted in `disable_when_zoomed`, navigating from a vim pane to another tmux pane normally causes the window to be unzoomed.
Some users may prefer the behavior of tmux's `-Z` option to `select-pane`, which keeps the window zoomed if it was zoomed.

This option enables that behavior.

Naturally, if `disable_when_zoomed` is enabled, this option will have no effect.

options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.save_on_switch
options.description:
You can configure the plugin to write the current buffer, or all buffers, when navigating from vim to tmux.

null: don't save on switch (default value)
1: `:update` (write the current buffer, but only if changed)
2: `:wall` (write all buffers)

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.description:
The configuration options for **vim-matchup** without the `matchup_` prefix.

For example, the following settings are equivialent to these `:setglobal` commands:
- `foo_bar = 1` -> `:setglobal matchup_foo_bar=1`
- `hello = "world"` -> `:setglobal matchup_hello="world"`
- `some_toggle = true` -> `:setglobal matchup_some_toggle`
- `other_toggle = false` -> `:setglobal nomatchup_other_toggle`

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_count_fail
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
When disabled (default), giving an invalid count to the `|[%|` and `|]%|` motions and the text
objects `|i%|` and `|a%|` will cause the motion or operation to fail.

When enabled, they will move as far as possible.

Note: targeting high counts when this option is enabled can become slow because many positions
need to be tried before giving up.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_nomids
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
If set to `1`, middle words (like `return`) are not matched to start and end words for
highlighting and motions.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_noskips
options.type: null or one of 0, 1, 2 or raw lua code
options.description:
This option controls whether matching is done within strings and comments.

- By default, it is set to `0` which means all valid matches are made within strings and
  comments.
- If set to `1`, symbols like `()` will still be matched but words like `for` and `end` will
  not.
- If set to `2`, nothing will be matched within strings and comments.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_start_plaintext
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
When enabled (the default), the plugin will be loaded for all buffers, including ones without
a file type set.

This allows matching to be done in new buffers and plain text files but adds a small start-up
cost to vim.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_stopline
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
Configures the number of lines to search in either direction while using motions and text
objects.
Does not apply to match highlighting (see `matchparen_stopline` instead).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to `0` to disable the plugin entirely.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.mappings_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to `0` to disable all mappings.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Deferred highlighting improves cursor movement performance (for example, when using `|hjkl|`)
by delaying highlighting for a short time and waiting to see if the cursor continues moving.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_fade_time
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
When set to `{time}` in milliseconds, the deferred highlighting behavior is changed in two
ways:

1. Highlighting of matches is preserved for at least `{time}` even when the cursor is moved
  away.
2. If the cursor stays on the same match for longer than `{time}`, highlighting is cleared.

The effect is that highlighting occurs momentarily and then disappears, regardless of where
the cursor is.
It is possible that fading takes longer than `{time}`, if vim is busy doing other things.

This value should be greater than the deferred show delay.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_hide_delay
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
If the cursor has not stopped moving, assume highlight is stale after this many milliseconds.

Stale highlights are hidden.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_show_delay
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
Delay, in milliseconds, between when the cursor moves and when we start checking if the cursor
is on a match.

Applies to both making highlights and clearing them for deferred highlighting.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
This option can disable match highlighting at `|startup|`.

Note: vim's built-in plugin `|pi_paren|` plugin is also disabled.
The variable `g:loaded_matchparen` has no effect on match-up.

You can also enable and disable highlighting for specific buffers using the variable
`|b:matchup_matchparen_enabled|`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_end_sign
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Configure the virtual symbol shown for closeless matches in languages like C++ and python.

```cpp
if (true)
  cout << "";
else
  cout << ""; ◀ if
```

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_hi_background
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Highlight buffer background between matches.
This uses the `MatchBackground` highlighting group and is linked to `ColorColumn` by default.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_hi_surround_always
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Always highlight the surrounding words, if possible.
This is like `|<plug>(matchup-hi-surround)|` but is updated each time the cursor moves.

This requires deferred matching (`matchparen_deferred = 1`).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_insert_timeout
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: Adjust the timeouts in milliseconds for highlighting.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_nomode
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
When not empty, match highlighting will be disabled in the specified modes, where each mode
is a single character like in the `|mode()|` function.

E.g., to disable highlighting in insert mode,
```nix
matchparen_nomode = "i";
```
and in visual modes,
```nix
matchparen_nomode = "vV\<c-v>";
```

Note: In visual modes, this takes effect only after moving the cursor.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen
options.type: null or (open submodule of attribute set of anything)
options.description:
Attrs controlling the behavior with off-screen matches.
If empty, this feature is disabled.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.border
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or list of string
options.description:
For floating window on neovim only: set to add a border.
If the value is the integer `1`, default borders are enabled.

A list or string can be specified as described in `|nvim_open_win()|`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.fullwidth
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: For `"popup"` method: make the floating window as wide as the current window.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.highlight
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
For popup method on vim only: set to a highlight group to override the colors in the
popup window.
The default is to use `*hl-Pmenu*`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.method
options.description:
Sets the method to use to show off-screen matches.
Possible values are:

- `"status"` (default): Replace the |status-line| for off-screen matches.\
  If a match is off of the screen, the line belonging to that match will be displayed
  syntax-highlighted in the status line along with the line number (if line numbers
  are enabled).
  If the match is above the screen border, an additional `Δ` symbol will be shown to
  indicate that the matching line is really above the cursor line.
- `"status_manual"`: Compute the string which would be displayed in the status-line or
  popup, but do not display it.
  The function `MatchupStatusOffscreen()` can be used to get the text.
- `"popup"`: Use a floating window to show the off-screen match.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.scrolloff
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
When enabled, off-screen matches will not be shown in the statusline while the cursor is
at the screen edge (respects the value of `'scrolloff'`).

This is intended to prevent flickering while scrolling with `j` and `k`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.syntax_hl
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
For popup method on vim only: syntax highlight the code in the popup.
May have performance implications.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_pumvisible
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
If set to `1`, matches will be made even when the `|popupmenu-completion|` is visible.

If you use an auto-complete plugin which interacts badly with matching, set this option to
`0`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_singleton
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Whether or not to highlight recognized words even if there is no match.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_stopline
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
The number of lines to search in either direction while highlighting matches.

Set this conservatively since high values may cause performance issues.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_timeout
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: Adjust the timeouts in milliseconds for highlighting.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_cursor_end
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
If enabled, cursor will land on the end of mid and close words while moving downwards
(`|%|/|]%|`).
While moving upwards (`|g%|`, `|[%|`) the cursor will land on the beginning.
Set to `0` to disable.

Note: this has no effect on operators: `d%` will delete `|inclusive|` of the ending word (this
is compatible with matchit).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to `0` to disable motions (`|matchup-%|`, `|%|`, `|[%|`, `|]%|`).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_override_Npercent
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description:
In vim, `{count}%` goes to the `{count}` percentage in the file (see `|N%|`).
match-up overrides this motion for small `{count}` (by default, anything less than 7).

- For example, to allow `{count}%` for `{count}` less than 12, set it to `11`.
- To disable this feature, and restore vim's default `{count}%`, set it to `0`.
- To always enable this feature, use any value greater than 99.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.mouse_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to `0` to disable selecting matches with double click.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.override_vimtex
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
By default, match-up is disabled for tex files when the plugin `|vimtex|` is detected.

To enable match-up for tex files, set this option to `1`.
This will replace vimtex's built-in highlighting and `%` map.

Note: matching may be computationally intensive for complex LaTeX documents.
If you experience slowdowns, consider also setting `matchparen_deferred` to `1`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.surround_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Enables the surround module which provides maps `|ds%|` and `|cs%|`.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.text_obj_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to `0` to disable text objects (`|a%|`, `|i%|`).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.text_obj_linewise_operators
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Modifies the set of operators which may operate line-wise with `|i%|` (see
`|matchup-feat-linewise|`).

You may use `"v"`, `"V"`, and `"\<c-v>"` (i.e., an actual CTRL-V character) to specify the
corresponding visual mode.

You can also specify custom plugin operators with 'g@' and optionally, an expression separated
by a comma.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.transmute_enabled
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Set to 1 to enable the experimental transmute feature (`|matchup-transmute|`).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.treesitter
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.description: Options provided to the treesitter matchup integration.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.treesitter.disable
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Languages for which to disable this module.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.treesitter.disable_virtual_text
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Do not use virtual text to highlight the virtual end of a block, for languages without
explicit end markers (e.g., Python).

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.treesitter.enable
options.description: Whether to enable treesitter integration.

options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.treesitter.include_match_words
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
Additionally include traditional vim regex matches for symbols.
For example, highlights `/* */` comments in C++ which are not supported in tree-sitter
matching.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.CloseOnExit
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Set this option to `1` to tell vimux to close the runner when you quit vim.

Caution: It is probably best not to mix this with `RunnerName`.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.CommandShell
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
- Set this option to `1` to enable shell completion in `PromptCommand`.
- Set this option to `0` to enable vim command editing in `PromptCommand`.

Enabling shell completion blocks the ability to use up-arrow to cycle through previously-run
commands in `PromptCommand`.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Debug
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.description:
If you're having trouble with vimux, set this option to get vimux to pass each tmux command to
`|echomsg|` before running it.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.ExpandCommand
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Should the command given at the prompt via `PromptCommand` be expanded using `expand()`.

Set to `1` to expand the string.

Unfortunately `expand()` only expands `%` (etc.) if the string starts with that character.
So the command is split at spaces and then rejoined after expansion.
With this simple approach things like `"%:h/test.xml"` are not possible.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Height
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The part of the screen the split pane Vimux will spawn should take up.
This option accepts both a number of lines/columns or a percentage.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.OpenExtraArgs
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Allows additional arguments to be passed to the tmux command that opens the runner.

Make sure that the arguments specified are valid depending on whether you're using panes or
windows, and your version of tmux.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Orientation
options.type: null or one of "v", "h" or raw lua code
options.description:
The default orientation of the split tmux pane.

This tells tmux to make the pane either vertically or horizontally, which is backward from
how Vim handles creating splits.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.PromptString
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The string presented in the vim command line when Vimux is invoked.

Be sure to put a space at the end of the string to allow for distinction between the prompt
and your input.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.ResetSequence
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The keys sent to the runner pane before running a command.

When vimux runs a tmux command, it first makes sure that the runner is not in copy mode by
running `copy-mode -q` on the runner.
This sequence is then sent to make sure that the runner is ready to receive input.

The default sends `C-u` to clear the line.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerName
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Setting the name for the runner.

Works for panes and windows.
This makes the VimuxRunner reusable between sessions.
Caveat is, all your instances (in the same session/window) use the same window.

Caution: It is probably best not to mix this with `CloseOnExit`.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerQuery
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Set this option to define a query to use for looking up an existing runner pane or window
when initiating Vimux.

Uses the tmux syntax for the target-pane and target-window command arguments.
(See the man page for tmux).

It must be an attrs containing up to two keys, `pane` and `window`, defining the query to
use for the respective runner types.

If no key exists for the current runner type, the search for an existing runner falls back
to the `UseNearest` option (and the related `RunnerName`).

If that option is false or either command fails, a new runner is created instead, positioned
according to `Orientation`.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerType
options.type: null or one of "pane", "window" or raw lua code
options.description:
The type of view object Vimux should use for the runner.

For reference, a tmux session is a group of windows, and a window is a layout of panes.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.TmuxCommand
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
The command that Vimux runs when it calls out to tmux.

It may be useful to redefine this if you're using something like tmate.

options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.UseNearest
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Use existing pane or window (not used by vim) if found instead of running `split-window`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.case_setting

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_motions
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
To remap any standard motion (`h`, `j`, `k`, `l`, `f`...) commands.

It can be useful if you use keyboard layouts other than QWERTY.

Valid motions that you can remap are:
```
h j k l w W b B e E ge gE , ; $ 0 ^ % \| f F t T
```

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_noremaps
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: To remap any key to normal! commands.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_remaps
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: To remap VM mappings to other VM mappings.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.default_mappings
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Default mappings are `permanent`, that is, always available, and applied when Vim starts.

Buffer mappings instead are applied per-buffer, when VM is started.
Permanent mappings, except `<C-n>`, can be disabled by setting this option to `0`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.disable_syntax_in_imode
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Whether to disable syntax highlighting in insert mode.

You could want to do it for performance reasons.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.filesize_limit
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.description: VM won't start if buffer size is greater than this.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.highlight_matches
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.description:
Controls VM default highlighting style for patterns matched, but not selected.

Possible useful values are `"underline"` and `"red"`.
Otherwise an empty string if you want the normal `|Search|` highlight, or a full highlight
command (help `|:hi|`).

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.insert_special_keys
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Some keys in insert mode can have a different behaviour, compared to vim
defaults. Possible values:

- `"c-a"`: `<C-A>` go to the beginning of the line, at indent level
- `"c-e"`: `<C-E>` go to the end of the line
- `"c-v"`: `<C-V>` paste from VM unnamed register

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.leader
options.description:
Mappings preceded by `\\` are meant prefixed with `|g:VM_leader|`.

Some of the permanent/visual mappings use the `|g:VM_leader|` as well, and you could want to
use a different one for them.
In this case you can define the leader as an attrs.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.live_editing
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Controls how often text is updated in insert mode.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.maps
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Customize key mappings.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.mouse_mappings
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: Whether to enable mouse mappings.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.persistent_registers
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
If true VM registers will be stored in the `|viminfo|`.
The `viminfo` option must include `!`, for this to work.

Also see `|:VMRegisters|`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.plugins_compatibilty
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description: Used for plugins compatibility, see `|vm-compatibility|`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.quit_after_leaving_insert_mode
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
So that you don't have to type `<Esc>` twice.

If you set this to `1`, maybe you can remap `Reselect Last`, so that you can quickly restart VM
with your last selection.
See `|vm-quick-reference|`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.recursive_operations_at_cursors
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
When executing normal commands in cursor mode (`dw` and similar), by default recursive mappings
are used, so that user text object can be used as well.

Set to `0` if you always want commands in cursor mode to be non-recursive.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.reindent_filetypes
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Autoindentation (via `|indentkeys|`) is temporarily disabled in insert mode, and you have to
reindent edited lines yoursef.

For filetypes included in this list, edited lines are automatically reindented when exiting
insert mode.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.reselect_first
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: The first region will be reselected after most commands, if set to `1`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.set_statusline
options.type: null or one of 1, 2, 3 or raw lua code
options.description:
Enable statusline when VM is active.
- With a value of `1`, the statusline will be set once, on VM start.
- With a value of `2`, the statusline will be refreshed on `|CursorHold|` event.
- With a value of `3`, also on `|CursorMoved|` event.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.show_warnings
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
When entering VM and there are mapping conflicts, a warning is displayed.

Set to `0` to disable this warning.
You can still run `|:VMDebug|` to see if there are conflicts.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.silent_exit
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Don't display a message when exiting VM.

You may prefer it if you already set up statusline integration.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.single_mode_auto_reset
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
If insert mode is entered while `|vm-single-mode|` is enabled, it will be reset automatically
when exiting insert mode, unless this value is `0`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.single_mode_maps
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
Set to `0` to disable entirely insert mode mappings to cycle cursors in `|vm-single-mode|`.

If you only want to change the default mappings, see `|vm-mappings-buffer|`.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.skip_empty_lines
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: When adding cursors up/down, skip empty lines.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.skip_shorter_lines
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description: When adding cursors up/down, skip shorter lines.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.use_first_cursor_in_line
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.description:
In insert mode, the active cursor is normally the last selected one.

Set this option to `1` to always use the first cursor in the line.

options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.user_operators
options.type: null or (list of (string or attribute set of (unsigned integer, meaning >=0) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.description:
Cursor mode only.

The elements of the list can be simple strings (then any text object can be accepted) or an
attrs with the operator as key, and the number of characters to be typed as value.

These operators can be either vim or plugin operators, mappings are passed recursively.

Note: `|vim-surround|` and `|vim-abolish|` have built-in support, this isn't needed for them
